# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Solaris Ridge for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it. It is short because the colony is small, and most of what happened here happened quietly.[/italic]
## Big Red LV-1413 is a red desert world of dust, rock and heat. Old hands call the settlement [bold]Big Red[/bold], after the colour that gets into your boots, your bunk and your lungs. Nobody came here for the view. They came because an independent outfit had bought the rights cheap and believed it could make the ground green.
## The Lichen - The plan was lichen. Seed the rock with hardy strains, let them break it down into soil and let the air follow over the decades. - A full atmosphere processor was beyond the founders' budget. The atmospherics condenser was built to keep the buildings breathable, never the sky. Nobody had proven lichen would work on a world like this one. - The greenhouse still stands from those years, and some of the old seed racks are still in it.
## When the Money Ran Out The lichen did not take. The dust storms stripped what little grew, sand ground down the machinery faster than parts could be shipped in, and every season the repair bill was larger than the last. The backers stopped answering. A mine was opened in the south western caves to cover the debt, and it was abandoned too. The independent venture ran out of money long before it ran out of people.
## The Quiet Sale - The colonization rights were sold to [bold]Weyland-Yutani[/bold] without a vote or an announcement. Most residents found out when the new logo appeared on their pay slips. - The Company built [bold]Lambda Lab[/bold] and [bold]Eta Lab[/bold] back into the caves, for biological storage and virology work, and put a checkpoint on the Lambda road. What is stored there is not discussed in this paper because we have never been told. - Everyone who stayed now works for the Company, whether they signed up for it or not.
## Today Around 120 people live on the Ridge. The reactor in the engineering complex keeps the lights on, the filtration plant keeps the water drinkable, and the marshal keeps the peace in a town where everyone knows everyone. Most off-worlders call it a dead end. The people who live here call it home anyway, and the Herald keeps the record for them.
